logical_model.summary: Logical design for datamodel, derived from the conceptual model. 20 entities carry 23 relationships: 2 associative entities resolve many-to-many relationships and 2 entities are identified through a parent. 0 entities required a surrogate identifier because no business key was recorded. Attributes are typed against abstract domains and carry no platform-specific length, precision or storage.

subject_areas.name: Master Data
subject_areas.description: Reference data that describes entities used throughout the system — customers, products, suppliers, employees, and geographic locations.

subject_areas.name: Inventory & Warehousing
subject_areas.description: Management of stock levels, warehouse locations, and inventory tracking across distribution centers.

subject_areas.name: Sales & Ordering
subject_areas.description: Customer orders, sales transactions, order line items, and sales representative management.

subject_areas.name: Fulfillment & Logistics
subject_areas.description: Shipment tracking, delivery management, and product returns.

entities.name: Audit Log
entities.description: A system record of all database operations for compliance and troubleshooting.

entities.name: Category
entities.description: A product classification or type grouping similar products.

entities.name: City
entities.description: A municipality or locality within a state.

entities.name: Country
entities.description: A sovereign nation used to classify geographic locations.

entities.name: Customer
entities.description: A person or organization that purchases products from the business.

entities.name: Department
entities.description: An organizational unit within the company to which employees are assigned.

entities.name: Employee
entities.description: A person employed by the organization, potentially reporting to a manager within a department.

entities.name: Inventory
entities.description: The quantity of a product held at a specific warehouse, with tracking of reorder levels.

entities.name: Order
entities.description: A customer purchase transaction containing one or more line items, placed on a specific date and tracked to completion.

entities.name: Order Line Item
entities.description: A single product and quantity within an order, at a specific unit price.

entities.name: Payment
entities.description: A financial transaction settling a customer's order invoice.

entities.name: Product
entities.description: An item offered for sale, identified by SKU, with pricing and supplier relationships.

entities.name: Product Promotion Association
entities.description: Resolves the many-to-many relationship between Product and Promotion. Each occurrence records that one Product references one Promotion.

entities.name: Product Warehouse Association
entities.description: Resolves the many-to-many relationship between Product and Warehouse. Each occurrence records that one Product references one Warehouse.

entities.name: Promotion
entities.description: A marketing campaign or discount offer that can be applied to products.

entities.name: Return Order
entities.description: A product returned by a customer from a placed order, with reason documented.

entities.name: Shipment
entities.description: The fulfillment and delivery of an order from a warehouse, with tracking information.

entities.name: State
entities.description: A province or administrative region within a country.

entities.name: Supplier
entities.description: A vendor that provides products to the business.

entities.name: Warehouse
entities.description: A physical distribution center or storage facility where inventory is held.

relationships.name: Order to Order Line Item
relationships.derived_from: conceptual relationship 'Order references Order Line Item'

relationships.name: Product to Order Line Item
relationships.derived_from: conceptual relationship 'Product references Order Line Item'

normalization_actions.action: Resolved many-to-many between Product and Promotion
normalization_actions.rationale: A many-to-many relationship cannot be represented without a repeating group. An associative entity keyed on both parents removes the repetition and gives the relationship a place to carry its own attributes later.

normalization_actions.action: Resolved many-to-many between Product and Warehouse
normalization_actions.rationale: A many-to-many relationship cannot be represented without a repeating group. An associative entity keyed on both parents removes the repetition and gives the relationship a place to carry its own attributes later.

normalization_actions.action: Checked non-key attributes against the full composite key
normalization_actions.rationale: Inventory has a composite key, so every non-key attribute (quantity, reorder_level) must depend on the whole key rather than part of it. No partial dependency was found.

normalization_actions.action: Identified Inventory as dependent on Warehouse
normalization_actions.rationale: Its business key includes Warehouse's key (warehouse_name), so it cannot be identified independently. The relationship is identifying and the key is propagated rather than duplicated.

normalization_actions.action: Checked non-key attributes against the full composite key
normalization_actions.rationale: Order Line Item has a composite key, so every non-key attribute (quantity, unit_price) must depend on the whole key rather than part of it. No partial dependency was found.

normalization_actions.action: Identified Order Line Item as dependent on Order
normalization_actions.rationale: Its business key includes Order's key (order_id), so it cannot be identified independently. The relationship is identifying and the key is propagated rather than duplicated.

normalization_actions.action: Confirmed State attributes are not repeated on City
normalization_actions.rationale: City references State, which references Country. The chain is already decomposed, so Country's attributes reach City by navigation rather than by duplication.

normalization_actions.action: Confirmed City attributes are not repeated on Customer
normalization_actions.rationale: Customer references City, which references State. The chain is already decomposed, so State's attributes reach Customer by navigation rather than by duplication.

normalization_actions.rationale: Shipment references Order, which references Employee. The chain is already decomposed, so Employee's attributes reach Shipment by navigation rather than by duplication.
